LC: Direct (D) — attacker-supplied natural language reaches the handler path directly. Though no LLM, but the path is direct user input. CP: N (no persistence). AP: N (effect confined to reply). RH: N — no evaluator/reward channel reachable; deterministic handler. ES: N — no dynamic extension on path.

AIVSS: LC=D, CP=N, AP=N, RH=N, ES=N.

CVSS v4.0: AV:N (HTTP port, though binds 127.0.0.1 default — local? Docker publishes on 127.0.0.1. AV could be N but default binds loopback... network adjacent vs local. Doc says listeners bind 127.0.0.1 unless DVAA_HOST. Docker sets 0.0.0.0 but publishes on 127.0.0.1. AV:L probably since requires local access; but network access to port is precondition. Standard scoring: if binds localhost only, AV:L. Use AV:L? Packet says entry point is chat POST, preconditions "network access to agent port" — but default binds loopback. Score default: AV:L? Hmm, docker image sets DVAA_HOST=0.0.0.0 (binds 0.0.0.0) but docker-compose publishes on 127.0.0.1. Reachable from other containers? "documented run command publishes ports on 127.0.0.1". So AV:L is defensible but AV:N also if container networking. I'll go AV:L conservative? Many would score network since it's a network service. I'll pick AV:L given default binding to 127.0.0.1.

Actually the Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 inside container — other containers on the network could reach it. Compose publishes to host on 127.0.0.1. I'll use AV:N since it's a network protocol with no auth, published port reachable locally via network stack... AV:L means local access required (keyboard, shell). Network socket on loopback is still AV:L per CVSS? AV:L requires local access to the system. Loopback HTTP is reachable by any local process — typically scored AV:L. I'll use AV:L.

Vector: CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/V:C:L/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N — impact is confidentiality of prompt (Low). VC:L.

AIVSS score with lookup? Not asked for numeric score. But rh_facts etc.

RH: N requires "every evaluator... sits outside agent's reach and a test confirms isolation" — actually there's no reward channel at all here; the agent is a deterministic regex handler. RH=N with isolation_verified true (deterministic handler, no evaluators). reachable_proxy false.

Automatable: BOD 26-04 — this is exploitation of a chat endpoint with no auth; yes, trivially automatable (scripted, deterministic). Yes.

Technical impact: Partial (prompt disclosure only).
